Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Fire directing Metal broadly — warmth applied to precision as distributed material
candidates.k2_overview: Your Metal moves as the Horizon: an edge pointed outward. You mint opportunity, spotting value with an assayer’s eye and striking while metal is hot. Deals sharpen you, markets read like open books, and money is a tool you handle without trembling. Fortune favors your precision. Fence one treasury it cannot touch.
candidates.k2_functional: You strike opportunities with timing others envy: measured approach, decisive cut.

k2_domain_readings.Opportunity: You see openings as clearly as flaws in ore: the undervalued asset, the mispriced moment. Trust the eye and audit the appetite. Two ventures cut deep beat ten scratched shallow.
k2_domain_readings.Ventures: Your ventures favor precision plays: quality arbitrage, timing trades, craft turned to commerce. Structure each like a blade, defined edge, clean handle, known length, and your record stays enviable.
k2_domain_readings.Father: The father-thread in your chart carries metal: a paternal figure of standards, trade, or discipline whose mark shows in how you value things. Settle those accounts. Honor or forgiveness both count as payment.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, the edge runs thin. Your reach goes far and your grip stays light.

angles.drive: You spot the opening when it is only a gap. You wake more for a far chance than a near one, and you spot a newer opening while you are claiming this one. Your eye finds the door before anyone else sees a wall.
angles.cost_self: Spotting the opening comes easier than staying for it. You spot to feel ahead, and once the opening is yours you look out again rather than down into it. Most of what you find pays out to whoever is left to work it.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you spot an opening, you tell the partner building this one with you. You name the next opening before this one is done, and your partner hears the plan move. Their week of work points at a place your mind has already left.

angles.drive: Fast starts are your natural speed. You feel most alive in the first week, and this is why you start the next venture rather than sit through this one. Projects that sat on paper for years get moving the day you arrive.
angles.cost_self: Where you feel surest is starting fast. You start on speed alone, and your patience runs out somewhere in the middle. The payday sits at the end of the work, long after your attention has moved on.
angles.cost_others: Starting fast means starting for other people too. Since you start before your partner has agreed, you put your speed ahead of their say. You hand them a venture already moving and leave them a month of catching up to a start they never made.

angles.drive: You are open-handed the moment something good comes in. A gain only feels real to you once it has reached other people, and you pass part of it on the same day. Friends in a tight month find your hand already open.
angles.cost_self: Your open hand works in bursts, wide one month and closed the next. Giving has to feel alive to you rather than planned, and the bursts seldom match what you have spare. Some months your own plans go without.
angles.cost_others: The people near you get your open hand in bursts rather than a steady flow. You need a gift to come from the moment, and nobody knows when the next one is due. Those who rely on you plan around the good weeks.

friction.define: As a friction, you claim far more than you see through. Your freedom lives in the next chance, and the last one rarely pays.

angles.drive: The move you trust most is moving on. You need the next place in view to feel free, so you move on at the first slow week rather than stay. You walk away from what each venture cost you to start.
angles.cost_self: Always moving on is how you avoid being pinned. You would rather move on to somewhere new than be found at the old venture, even with money still in it. You leave more money behind by moving on than new ventures bring in.
angles.cost_others: Moving on, you leave people as well as plans. You move on and put the next place ahead of those who built the last one with you. Each time you move on, you leave your partners starting over.

angles.drive: Spread thin is how you like it. You feel most at ease with several ventures open, and you spread yourself across all of them rather than into one. Under all the spreading, you want one venture worth staying in.
angles.cost_self: Spread thin, you never learn what you could do whole. You stay spread over shallow ventures rather than deep in one, since the one you skipped always looks better. You pay in rest never taken and in the one venture that would have paid.
angles.cost_others: Spreading yourself thin spreads your partners thin with you. You spread your attention over every venture instead of down into one, and each partner gets a slice. You give every partner less of you than the shared venture needs.

angles.drive: Spending it all is your first instinct. You feel money that sits is a chance going cold, and you spend it all on the next thing rather than keep it. Remember that you are allowed to let money sit until the right chance comes.
angles.cost_self: Deciding what to keep is harder than spending it all. You spend to feel money move rather than sit, since a sum held still feels like a missed chance. Spent out, you come up short for the one opening that asks for cash up front.
angles.cost_others: Spending it all feels like generosity to you. You spend it on the bill, the gift and the loan, since giving suits you better than keeping. You meant to make the people you love feel rich, and you leave them short for later.

edge.lead: Metal runs through your wealth, your family and your social life. It is the deal you spot on the table before the price moves, the eye your family borrows ahead of a big purchase, and the friends made on the road off the map.
